To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FocalScan is an algorithm that identifies cancer genes by integrating DNA and RNA expression data.

we have developed a tool that can scan a genome to identify regions of focal copy number gain or loss that are associated with coordinated changes in RNA expression, thus identifying potential cancer drivers and suppressors.
FocalScan is a novel method for finding altered genes in cancer that combines copy number alteration and RNA expression data and is capable of scanning the whole genome unaided.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a tool for the identification of genes altered by copy number change and coordinated expression change in cancer, and we believe that this tool can be of use to the cancer community.
the integration of genomic and transcriptional data to find cancer genes, and the development of a tool to facilitate such analysis.
the identification of genes that are altered in cancer and contribute to the malignant phenotype of the tumor cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FocalScan is an effective tool for identifying cancer genes based on coordinated DNA-RNA change.

FocalScan is the most accurate tool for identifying focal copy number alterations in cancer, and it is the first tool that can identify focal copy number alterations without the use of gene annotations.
FocalScan is a powerful tool that can be used to identify genes that are altered in cancer based on their coordinated copy number and RNA change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method that can identify cancer driver genes by integrating DNA and RNA data.
FocalScan is the first tool that integrates copy number and RNA data to identify cancer drivers in a genome-wide fashion, and that it outperforms other methods on this task.
FocalScan provides a powerful and flexible approach to identify focal genomic regions that are likely to harbor cancer drivers or suppressor genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of DNA and RNA data, in particular the latter in its full transcriptomic complexity, is necessary to uncover all cancer drivers and suppressors.
the integration of copy number and RNA-seq data provides a powerful tool for identifying cancer drivers or suppressor genes in cancer.
the integration of copy number and RNA sequencing data, while not a new concept, can be used in a novel way to identify focal regions that contain cancer driver genes.
